name: Woodway Hyperscale Data Center Pipeline

values.DataCenterNotes: Woodway's own announcement of September 22, 2026 says the pipeline will give dedicated gas transport capacity to a behind-the-meter power generation project for hyperscale data center development. The customer, the data center and the site are not named. A trade news report from September 2026 repeats this and says the pipeline has an option for extension. Woodway is based in Houston.

researcher_notes: Woodway Energy Infrastructure announced on September 22, 2026 that it signed definitive agreements to develop, build, own and run a 22-mile, 30-inch gas pipeline. The pipeline gives dedicated capacity to a power plant behind the meter for hyperscale data center development. Service is expected in the first half of 2028, subject to regulatory approvals. This meets the data center add rule: a real pipeline project, described by its developer, that supplies energy to a data center. No existing row matches. The state is inferred, not stated. Woodway's own operating assets page lists only Texas pipelines (Bluebonnet in Bastrop, Colorado, Lee, Fayette and Lavaca counties, Comal County, and Goliad County), and Woodway is an intrastate pipeline operator based in Houston, so Texas is the likely state. A trade news report also says the company's assets are all in Texas. The county, the customer and the data center site were not found in the announcement, trade news or searches, and no Texas Railroad Commission filing for this line was found. The start and end places and the route are blank and the route accuracy is 'no route'. The pipeline name is a working name made from the announcement. The Woodway announcement and the BIC Magazine report are one story reprinted, and the Data Center Dynamics and W Media reports repeat the same release, so none is independent. Confidence is medium. Owner is spelled as the company spells it with its LLC form, and the ownership list has no existing match to reuse.
